# 📚 Comprehensive Documentation Suite for TimeCapsuleTV ## Summary This PR adds a complete documentation suite to make TimeCapsuleTV more accessible to new users and contributors. The changes include enhanced setup instructions, troubleshooting guides, API documentation, deployment options, and improved inline code documentation. **Key additions:** - **Enhanced README.md** with detailed setup instructions, system requirements, and quick troubleshooting - **CONTRIBUTING.md** with developer guidelines, project structure, and contribution workflow - **TROUBLESHOOTING.md** with platform-specific solutions and debugging steps - **API.md** with complete codebase documentation and extension examples - **DEPLOYMENT.md** covering deployment from desktop to cloud (Raspberry Pi, GitHub Pages, Netlify, etc.) - **CHANGELOG.md** documenting project evolution and technical milestones - **Enhanced inline documentation** in core classes with detailed docstrings The documentation provides comprehensive coverage from first-time setup through advanced deployment scenarios, making the project more maintainable and contributor-friendly. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human **Risk Level: 🟡 Medium** - Documentation accuracy is critical for user experience - [ ] **Test installation instructions** - Follow the README.md setup steps from scratch on a clean system to ensure they work correctly - [ ] **Verify troubleshooting solutions** - Check that common issues in TROUBLESHOOTING.md have accurate solutions (especially Chrome/WebDriver setup) - [ ] **Validate API documentation** - Ensure the API.md accurately reflects the actual code structure and method signatures in the codebase - [ ] **Check deployment instructions** - Verify that at least one deployment method (e.g., web version) works as documented **Recommended test plan:** 1. ## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: viperjuice
body:
## Summary
This PR implements the JSON/JSONL export functionality from Phase 5.2 of the ROADMAP.

### Features Added
- **JSON/JSONL Export Classes**: `JSONExporter` and `JSONLExporter` with full functionality
- **Multiple Schema Types**: 4 formats (flat, nested, minimal, full)
- **Streaming Support**: Memory-efficient JSONL streaming for large files
- **Compression**: Gzip compression for both JSON and JSONL outputs
- **Relationship Tracking**: Enhanced CodeChunk with unique IDs and parent-child relationships
- **CLI Integration**: New options: --format, --schema, --output, --compress

### Changes
- Updated `chunker/chunker.py` to track parent-child relationships
- Created export module in `chunker/export/`
- Enhanced CLI with export options
- Added 18 comprehensive tests

### Testing
All 96 tests passing, including 18 new tests for export functionality.

### Usage Examples
```bash
# Export as JSON with nested schema
python cli/main.py file.py -l python --format json --schema nested -o output.json

# Export as compressed JSONL
python cli/main.py file.py -l python --format jsonl --compress -o output.jsonl

# Stream large files efficiently
python cli/main.py large_file.py -l python --format jsonl -o output.jsonl
```

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The anticheat system was encountering runtime errors due to incorrect usage of the `GetGroundZFor_3dCoord` function:

```
SCRIPT ERROR: @miniature-octo-adventure/client/core.lua:13: attempt to perform arithmetic on a boolean value (local 'groundZ')
> CheckIfEntityOnGround (@miniature-octo-adventure/client/core.lua:13)
> handler (@miniature-octo-adventure/client/core.lua:80)
```

## Root Cause

The `GetGroundZFor_3dCoord` function in FiveM returns **two values**:
1. A boolean indicating whether ground was found
2. The Z coordinate of the ground (only valid when the first value is `true`)

The code was incorrectly capturing only the first return value (boolean) and then attempting arithmetic operations on it:

```lua
-- BEFORE (incorrect)
local groundZ = GetGroundZFor_3dCoord(position.x, position.y, position.z, false)
return math.abs(position.z - groundZ) <= groundThreshold  -- Error: groundZ is boolean!
```

## Solution

Fixed the function calls to properly capture both return values and added appropriate validation:

```lua
-- AFTER (correct)
local found, groundZ = GetGroundZFor_3dCoord(position.x, position.y, position.z, false)
if not found then
    return false  -- Ground not found, assume not on ground
end
return math.abs(position.z - groundZ) <= groundThreshold  -- Safe: groundZ is numeric
```

## Files Changed

- **`client/core.lua`**: Fixed `CheckIfEntityOnGround` function (line 9)
- **`client/monitoring.lua`**: Fixed `CheckCollisionBypass` function (line 322)

## Impact

- ✅ Eliminates script errors that were spamming the console
- ✅ Maintains all existing functionality 
- ✅ Improves robustness when ground detection fails
- ✅ No breaking changes to the anticheat system

This is a minimal, surgical fix that addresses the specific runtime error without affecting any other parts of the codebase.

author: boatsmcgee
body:
Resolves #547
Resolves #760

## Overview

Users on Linux are limited by the amount of file descriptors that can be opened by a single `mkvmerge` process (or the user itself). A workaround of setting the `-ulimit -n` value to one that well exceeds the total number of chunks to merge and performing the merge manually is not a long-term solution and may not work for all environments. Instead, the chunks can be merged into groups of 100 chunks that are then merged into the final output. This group size should be well within reasonable limits.

Additionally, the `String::with_capacity(VALUE)` has been adjusted to account for varying input lengths. I merely printed the capacity (in bytes) before and the length (returns bytes) afterwards to ensure there was no reallocation occurring when writing to the `file_string`.

### Testers Wanted

I have not tested the failure case on Linux, only Windows. Windows either has no such limit or I have yet to reach it in my testing. If you have encountered this issue or are willing to test with an environment where the `ulimit -n` is set very low, please give this PR a try to make absolutely sure this avoids the `ulimit` issue.

### Potential Improvements

Group sizes could be determined by checking the `ulimit -n` value rather than hardcoding to 100.

Currently, the groups are executed linearly but could be parallelized with threads assuming `ulimit` only applies to a single process rather than the entire shell or user environment.

The groups are redundant and could be deleted, keeping the temporary folder disk usage low.

The merging preprocess is ephemeral and video files can be very large. To reduce disk thrashing, the groups should be stored in memory until the final output is merged and written to the disk. Doing so across platforms is a difficult task in and of itself and could be even more difficult if no such solution exists for Rust.

Thank you,
\- Boats M.

- manage drafting prompt
- allow users to edit and send generated drafts
- show emails awaiting a human in the UI

## Testing
- `npm run lint`
- `python -m py_compile daemon-service/*.py web-app/api/api.py`

## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive test coverage for both the sync and async implementations of the accounts module, significantly improving test robustness, error handling validation, and edge case coverage.

## Changes Overview

### Test Coverage Improvements

#### Async Module (src/accounts/async.rs):
- **Before**: 11 tests
- **After**: 24 tests (+13 new tests)
- **New test code**: ~347 lines

#### Sync Module (src/accounts/sync.rs):  
- **Before**: 11 tests
- **After**: 21 tests (+10 new tests)
- **New test code**: ~320 lines

### Total Coverage Statistics
- **Total tests**: 45 (up from 22)
- **Total new test code**: ~667 lines
- **Coverage areas**: Version checking, error handling, edge cases, parameter validation, concurrency, lifecycle management

## New Test Categories

### Version Checking & Error Handling
- **Server version compatibility**: Tests all functions reject requests when server version is too old
- **Error response handling**: Tests empty responses, no responses, invalid inputs
- **Parse error handling**: Tests invalid timestamps, malformed data

### Parameter Validation & Edge Cases  
- **Boundary conditions**: Tests edge case contract IDs (0, i32::MAX)
- **Parameter combinations**: Tests all valid parameter combinations for multi-parameter functions
- **Empty input handling**: Tests empty tags, null parameters

### Concurrency & Lifecycle (Async)
- **Concurrent subscriptions**: Tests multiple simultaneous subscriptions don't interfere  
- **Subscription cleanup**: Tests proper resource cleanup when subscriptions are dropped
- **Stream handling**: Tests continuous data stream processing

## Test Results

All tests pass successfully:
- Async tests: 24/24 passing
- Sync tests: 21/21 passing  
- Code passes clippy checks with no warnings
- All code properly formatted

## Impact

- ✅ **Backward Compatible**: All existing functionality preserved
- ✅ **Comprehensive Coverage**: Major error scenarios and edge cases now tested
- ✅ **Quality Assurance**: Enhanced error handling validation
- ✅ **Maintainability**: Well-documented test cases for future development

author: viperjuice
body:
## Summary

This PR implements Phase 5.1 (Advanced CLI Features) and Phase 5.3 (User Experience) from the project roadmap, significantly enhancing the CLI capabilities for processing codebases at scale.

## ✨ Features Added

### 🚀 Batch Processing
- **Directory input support**: Process entire directories with `batch` command
- **Glob patterns**: Use `--pattern "*.py"` to match files
- **Stdin input**: Pipe file lists with `--stdin` flag
- **Parallel processing**: Configure workers with `--parallel` (defaults to CPU count)
- **Recursive/non-recursive**: Control directory traversal with `--recursive/--no-recursive`

### 🎯 File Filtering & Selection
- **Include/exclude patterns**: `--include "*.py" --exclude "*test*"`
- **Chunk type filtering**: `--types "function_definition,class_definition"`
- **Size-based filtering**: `--min-size 5 --max-size 100` (lines)
- **Auto-language detection**: Automatically detects language from file extensions

### 📊 Progress Tracking & UX
- **Rich progress bars**: Visual feedback with ETA for batch operations
- **Quiet mode**: `--quiet` flag suppresses progress output
- **Summary statistics**: Shows chunk counts by language and type
- **Multiple output formats**:
  - Table format (default) with rich formatting
  - JSON output with `--json`
  - JSONL streaming format with `--jsonl`

### ⚙️ Configuration Support
- **`.chunkerrc` files**: TOML configuration for all CLI options
- **Hierarchical loading**: Searches current directory, then home directory
- **Example provided**: `.chunkerrc.example` demonstrates all options
- **Full option support**: All CLI flags can be configured

### 🆕 Additional Commands
- **`languages` command**: Lists all available languages
- **Enhanced `chunk` command**: Now supports all filtering options

## 🧪 Testing

- Added comprehensive test suite: `tests/test_cli.py`
- **16 tests** covering all new features
- All tests passing ✅
- Test categories:
  - Configuration loading
  - File pattern matching
  - File processing with filters
  - CLI command integration
  - Batch operations

## 📖 Usage Examples

```bash
# Process all Python files in a directory
python cli/main.py batch src/ --include "*.py" --exclude "*test*"

# Process with specific chunk types and size limits
python cli/main.py batch . --types "function_definition" --min-size 10 --max-size 200

# Use glob patterns with parallel processing
python cli/main.py batch --pattern "**/*.rs" --parallel 8 --json > chunks.json

# Process files from stdin
find . -name "*.py"  < /dev/null |  python cli/main.py batch --stdin --quiet

# Use with config file
python cli/main.py batch src/ --config .chunkerrc
```

## 📁 Files Changed

- **`cli/main.py`** (+336 lines): Complete rewrite with new features
- **`tests/test_cli.py`** (new, 392 lines): Comprehensive test suite
- **`.chunkerrc.example`** (new, 29 lines): Example configuration file
- **`specs/ROADMAP.md`**: Updated completion status for Phase 5.1 & 5.3

## 🎯 Impact

This PR transforms the CLI from a simple single-file processor to a powerful batch processing tool suitable for analyzing entire codebases. The addition of filtering, parallel processing, and configuration support makes it production-ready for large-scale code analysis tasks.

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] All tests passing
- [x] Documentation updated (ROADMAP.md)
- [x] Example configuration provided
- [x] No breaking changes to existing functionality
- [x] Follows project coding standards

author: benchstr
harehare
body:
This change introduces the ability to use parentheses in expressions to control the order of evaluation. The parser has been updated to recognize parentheses and represent them as a `Paren` node in the AST. The evaluator has been updated to handle this new node type by recursively evaluating the expression within the parentheses.

- Added `Expr::Paren(Rc<Node>)` to the AST to represent parenthesized expressions.
- Modified the parser to handle `LParen` and `RParen` tokens, creating `Paren` nodes.
- Updated the evaluator to correctly evaluate `Paren` nodes.
- Added tests to ensure that expressions with parentheses are parsed and evaluated correctly.

Pull Request: speir-ticket.yml
Summary:
This PR introduces the speir-ticket.yml configuration file, establishing key workflows and deployment logic for the Speir Ticket and Event Management Platform.

Purpose:

Automate deployment and integration tasks specific to the Speir Ticket system.
Define CI/CD pipeline or event-triggered workflows.
Improve operational efficiency and reduce manual errors during ticketing updates or deployments.
What's Included:

Workflow triggers (e.g., push, pull_request, schedule)
Build/test/deploy jobs related to the ticketing platform
Secrets and environment variables (referenced securely)
Custom steps for:
Linting and validation of event schema
Deployment to staging/production environments
Integration with other Speir services (e.g., SADIS, Speir Pay, InterQ)
Benefits:

Enables streamlined releases for ticketing features.
Provides traceability and reproducibility across environments.
Supports future extensibility for event ticket sales, RFID check-ins, and real-time reporting.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

Previously, when the last player was kicked from a lobby, the lobby would remain in the system as an empty lobby until the periodic cleanup process removed it after the TTL timeout (30 minutes). This caused:

- Empty lobbies to persist unnecessarily in the system
- Potential confusion on the landing page where empty lobbies might briefly appear
- Inefficient resource usage

## Solution

This PR implements immediate removal of lobbies when they become empty after a player is kicked.

### Key Changes

1. **Enhanced `kick_player()` function** - Now checks if lobby becomes empty after removing a player and removes the lobby immediately
2. **Added immediate cleanup logic** - Empty lobbies are removed without waiting for the TTL timeout
3. **Improved API response** - Returns `{"lobby_removed": true}` when a kick results in lobby removal

### API Behavior

**Before:**
```bash
# Kick last player from lobby
curl -X POST /lobby/ABC123/kick -d '{"emoji":"🐶","host_token":"..."}'
# Response: {"status": "ok"}
# Lobby still exists but empty for up to 30 minutes
```

**After:**
```bash
# Kick last player from lobby  
curl -X POST /lobby/ABC123/kick -d '{"emoji":"🐶","host_token":"..."}'
# Response: {"status": "ok", "lobby_removed": true}
# Lobby removed immediately
```

### Frontend Impact

The landing page automatically reflects lobby removals through existing API endpoints:
- `/lobbies` - No longer returns removed lobbies
- `/lobbies/network` - Only shows lobbies with active players

### Testing

- ✅ Added comprehensive test coverage for empty lobby removal
- ✅ Updated existing tests to accommodate new behavior
- ✅ Manual API testing confirms immediate removal
- ✅ All 69 core server tests pass

### Example Usage

```python
# Create lobby and add player
lobby = create_lobby()
add_player(lobby, "🐶")

# Lobby exists with 1 player
assert lobby in active_lobbies()

# Kick the only player
kick_player(lobby, "🐶")

# Lobby is immediately removed
assert lobby not in active_lobbies()
```

This change ensures efficient resource management and provides a cleaner experience for users on the landing page.

body:
- Introduced `rescan_interval` as an optional field in the Project struct.
- Updated project creation and update methods to handle rescan intervals.
- Implemented a new rescan worker to periodically check for projects needing rescanning.
- Added database query logic to find projects that require rescanning based on their last indexed time and rescan interval.
- Created a HumanDuration type for better handling of human-readable duration strings.
- Updated server routes and request/response types to include rescan interval.
- Refactored task manager to remove old rescan logic and integrate with the new rescan worker.
- Added tests for rescan functionality, including edge cases and interval calculations.

author: uddhav
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements comprehensive quest enhancements that allow mobs to autonomously post and accept quests, creating a dynamic quest ecosystem where NPCs can interact with each other and players through the quest system.

## Features Implemented

### New Quest Types
- **AQ_PLAYER_KILL**: Mobs can post quests to eliminate player killers
- **AQ_MOB_KILL_BOUNTY**: Mobs can post bounty quests targeting specific hostile mobs

### Mob Quest Genetics System
Added two new genetics that control mob quest behavior:
- **GenQuest**: Controls a mob's tendency to accept quests (0-100)
- **GenAdventurer**: Controls a mob's adventurous tendency for exploration-based quests (0-100)

These can be configured in mob files:
```
GenQuest: 60
GenAdventurer: 70
```

### Mob Reputation System
- Mobs maintain a reputation score (0-100) that increases with successful quest completion
- Higher reputation mobs are more likely to receive challenging quests
- Reputation affects quest acceptance probability calculations

### Intelligent Quest Acceptance
Mobs evaluate quests based on multiple factors:
- Personal genetics (quest_tendency, adventurer_tendency)
- Character stats and level relative to quest difficulty
- Current reputation score
- Quest type compatibility (combat vs exploration)

### Quest Completion & Rewards
- Mobs receive gold, experience points, and items upon quest completion
- Reputation increases with successful completions
- Proper integration with existing combat and trigger systems

### Example Usage

A mob configured with high quest genetics will actively participate in the quest economy:

```
# In mob file
GenQuest: 80        # High interest in accepting quests
GenAdventurer: 60   # Moderate interest in exploration quests
```

This creates emergent gameplay where:
- A "Pacificador" mob might post a quest to kill troublesome thieves
- Adventurous mobs accept these quests for rewards and reputation
- Players can compete with or collaborate alongside quest-active NPCs

## Technical Implementation

- Extends existing mob AI system with minimal changes
- Integrates with current quest framework and questmaster system
- Adds quest processing to mobile activity loop (5% chance per tick)
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing quest system
- Tested with successful MUD startup and genetics loading verification

The implementation creates a living world where NPCs have their own motivations and can pursue goals independently, enhancing immersion and creating dynamic content for players.

Fixes #40.

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/compare/v4.2.1...v4.3.0)

This is Zod's biggest release since 4.0. It addresses several of Zod's longest-standing feature requests.

#### `z.fromJSONSchema()`

Convert JSON Schema to Zod ([#​5534](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/5534), [#​5586](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/5586))

You can now convert JSON Schema definitions directly into Zod schemas. This function supports JSON Schema `"draft-2020-12"`, `"draft-7"`, `"draft-4"`, and OpenAPI 3.0.

```typescript
import * as z from "zod";

const schema = z.fromJSONSchema({
  type: "object",
  properties: {
    name: { type: "string", minLength: 1 },
    age: { type: "integer", minimum: 0 },
  },
  required: ["name"],
});

schema.parse({ name: "Alice", age: 30 }); // ✅
```

The API should be considered experimental. There are no guarantees of 1:1 "round-trip soundness": `MySchema` > `z.toJSONSchema()` > `z.fromJSONSchema()`. There are several features of Zod that don't exist in JSON Schema and vice versa, which makes this virtually impossible.

Features supported:

- All primitive types (`string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `null`, `object`, `array`)
- String formats (`email`, `uri`, `uuid`, `date-time`, `date`, `time`, `ipv4`, `ipv6`, and more)
- Composition (`anyOf`, `oneOf`, `allOf`)
- Object constraints (`additionalProperties`, `patternProperties`, `propertyNames`)
- Array constraints (`prefixItems`, `items`, `minItems`, `maxItems`)
- `$ref` for local references and circular schemas
- Custom metadata is preserved

#### `z.xor()` — exclusive union ([#​5534](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/5534))

A new exclusive union type that requires **exactly one** option to match. Unlike `z.union()` which passes if *any* option matches, `z.xor()` fails if zero or more than one option matches.

```typescript
const schema = z.xor([z.string(), z.number()]);

schema.parse("hello"); // ✅

This pull request introduces enhancements to the `MiningSpeedRetrievalTask` for better parsing of mining speed values and refines location checks in the `GlacialMacro`'s `StartingState`. The most important changes include the addition of regex-based parsing for mining speed, improved error handling, and updating location validation logic.

### Improvements to mining speed retrieval:

* **Regex-based parsing for mining speed:** Introduced `MINING_SPEED_PATTERN` to extract numeric values (including decimals) from the "Mining Speed" string in the SkyBlock GUI. This replaces the previous approach of splitting strings, making the parsing more robust. (`src/main/java/com/jelly/mightyminerv2/feature/impl/AutoGetStats/tasks/impl/MiningSpeedRetrievalTask.java`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-55ee27a1458c643d0a29ae416ef0874a1e014c9d8fec0289d6b8f8a4927f78ffR22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-55ee27a1458c643d0a29ae416ef0874a1e014c9d8fec0289d6b8f8a4927f78ffL51-R73)
* **Improved error handling:** Enhanced error messages to include the problematic line and exception details when parsing fails, aiding debugging. (`src/main/java/com/jelly/mightyminerv2/feature/impl/AutoGetStats/tasks/impl/MiningSpeedRetrievalTask.java`, [src/main/java/com/jelly/mightyminerv2/feature/impl/AutoGetStats/tasks/impl/MiningSpeedRetrievalTask.javaL51-R73](diffhunk://#diff-55ee27a1458c643d0a29ae416ef0874a1e014c9d8fec0289d6b8f8a4927f78ffL51-R73))

### Refinements to location validation in `GlacialMacro`:

* **Updated location check logic:** Removed `SubLocation.GLACITE_TUNNELS` from the valid locations list, restricting checks to `SubLocation.DWARVEN_BASE_CAMP` for better alignment with macro requirements. (`src/main/java/com/jelly/mightyminerv2/macro/impl/GlacialMacro/states/StartingState.java`, [src/main/java/com/jelly/mightyminerv2/macro/impl/GlacialMacro/states/StartingState.javaL32-R32](diffhunk://#diff-85a2afecbc3942571c5385e8c1084e46d4bd23b6bb9424e6d695008560708c35L32-R32))

author: mellonmusk
body:
### 📌 개요
- 아직 재시도 로직, 스케줄링 처리가 추가되어야 함 (to be continued... don't merge yet) 
제가 까먹을까봐 임시로 올립니다

### 💌 To Everyone
환경변수 추가됨. pod마다 다르게 지정해야 함. application.yml 참고

## Issue
현재 AI 서버 → Spring 서버 → Kafka → (SSE/WebSocket) → 클라이언트 구조에서,
Pod가 2개 이상일 때 다른 Pod에서 메시지를 처리하면 클라이언트에 메시지가 도달하지 않는 문제가 발생하고 있습니다.
Kafka 메시지를 수신한 Pod가 해당 사용자의 SSE/WebSocket 세션을 보유하지 않아 메시지 전송에 실패합니다.
(SSE/WebSocket 세션 정보가 연결된 Pod의 로컬 메모리에만 저장되기 때문)

---

방식 1: 모든 Pod이 메시지 수신 후 필터링
Kafka의 group.id를 Pod마다 다르게 설정하여 모든 Pod이 메시지를 브로드캐스트 방식으로 수신하고, 자신이 보유한 userId 세션에만 메시지를 전송합니다.
(구조가 단순하고 안정적이지만, Pod 수 증가 시 불필요한 메시지 처리 비용이 커짐)

---

방식 2: userId → Pod 라우팅 테이블 기반 메시지 전달
각 userId가 연결된 Pod 정보를 Redis 등의 In-Memory DB에 저장하고,
Kafka 메시지를 해당 Pod로만 라우팅하여 메시지를 전송합니다.
(리소스 낭비는 줄일 수 있지만, 라우팅 정보의 정합성 유지 관리, 실패 대응 로직이 추가로 필요함)
동작 과정:
1. SSE/WebSocket 연결 시:
사용자 A가 Pod X에 SSE/WebSocket 연결을 시도합니다.

Pod X는 연결 성공 후, Redis에 pod정보 저장(사용자가 연결된 Pod을 식별합니다.)

2. Kafka 메시지 수신 시:
Kafka 컨슈머 Pod (예: Pod Y)가 Kafka 토픽에서 사용자 A에 대한 메시지를 수신합니다.

Pod Y는 Redis에서 사용자 A가 연결된 Pod의 정보를 조회합니다.

3. 메시지 라우팅 및 전송:
Pod Y는 조회된 파드 정보로 직접 내부 HTTP를 통해 메시지를 전송합니다.

Pod X는 해당 내부 호출을 받으면, 자신이 보유한 사용자 A의 SSE/WebSocket 세션으로 메시지를 푸시합니다.

---

방식 3:
SSE/WebSocket 처리만 전담하는 Gateway Pod를 두고, 모든 클라이언트 연결을 여기에 몰아주는 방식

AI 서버 → Kafka → Gateway → 클라이언트 구조로 변경.

이 경우 WebSocket 세션이 하나의 컴포넌트에 집중되므로 Pod 간 메시지 전달 문제가 사라짐, Spring Boot 애플리케이션을 2개로 분리해야 함:
- Gateway 서비스

WebSocket/SSE endpoint만 존재

Kafka consumer or REST endpoint 보유

Redis 등으로 유저 세션 상태 관리

- 비즈니스 서비스

Kafka producer, 비즈니스 로직 처리

WebSocket에 전혀 관여하지 않음 

---
방식 2로 하기로 했습니다. 카카오 멘토님께서도 실무에서 In-Memory DB(Redis 등)를 활용한 라우팅 구조가 많이 사용된다고 하셨습니다.
그래서 방식 1로 했던 commit을 다시 revert했습니다.

## ✅ 체크 리스트

- [x] PR이 관련 이슈를 정확히 참조하고, 적절한 라벨을 선택했습니다.

author: aerolakshyam
body:
This pull request completely replaces the backend server implementation with a React landing page component.

Changes made:
- Removed Express.js server setup and SQLite database configuration
- Removed all database table creation and sample data insertion
- Removed all API endpoints for users, skills, profiles, and admin functionality
- Replaced with a React functional component implementing a landing page
- Added React hooks (useState, useEffect) for scroll animations and visibility tracking
- Implemented responsive design with Tailwind CSS classes
- Added interactive UI elements including navigation, hero section, features, stats, services, and call-to-action
- Integrated Lucide React icons for visual elements
- Added CSS animations and transitions for enhanced user experience
- Included React Router navigation functionality

The file has been transformed from a Node.js backend server (943 lines) to a React frontend component (1280 lines).

author: vmoroz
body:
### Overview

This PR centralizes Windows build configuration, improves build script maintainability, and resolves several security and build issues.

### 🔧 Build System Improvements

**Centralized Windows Configuration**
- Created `HermesWindows.cmake` to consolidate Windows-specific build logic
- Moved compiler flags, linker options, and platform detection from scattered locations
- Unified ARM64/ARM64EC handling and cross-compilation logic
- Simplified CMakePresets.json by removing embedded flags

**Enhanced Build Script (`build.js`)**
- Added `--targets` parameter for selective builds (e.g., `--targets hermesc,libshared`)
- Improved argument parsing with better validation
- Enhanced error handling and logging
- Fixed ARM64EC compiler selection logic

### 🛡️ Security & Compliance Fixes

**BinSkim Security Issues**
- Added proper security flags (`/guard:cf`, `/GS`, `/DYNAMICBASE`, `/ZH:SHA_256`)
- Configured deterministic builds with `/BREPRO`
- Added CET compatibility for supported platforms
- Implemented conditional flag application based on target architecture

**MSVC Warning/Error Resolution**
- Fixed C4703 "potentially uninitialized variable" errors in external dtoa library
- Resolved conflicts between `/sdl` security flags and external code
- Improved warning suppression for third-party dependencies

### 🧹 Code Quality Improvements

**JavaScript Build Scripts**
- Added ESLint and Prettier configuration for consistent code style
- Added formatting and linting commands to the new package.json
- Added comprehensive .gitignore for `node_modules`
- Created detailed README with usage instructions

**CMake Fixes**
- Fixed incorrect `DEPENDS` usage in `add_custom_command(TARGET ...)`
- Improved cross-platform build detection
- Enhanced variable scope handling in CMake functions

### 📁 New Files
- package.json - Node.js dependencies and scripts
- eslint.config.js - ESLint configuration
- .prettierrc - Prettier formatting rules
- .gitignore - Git ignore for build artifacts
- README.md - Documentation for build scripts
- HermesWindows.cmake - Centralized Windows build logic

### 🎯 Benefits
- **Security**: Resolves BinSkim security compliance issues
- **Maintainability**: Centralized Windows build configuration reduces duplication
- **Developer Experience**: Better build script formatting and selective target building
- **Reliability**: Fixed various build system edge cases and warnings

### ✅ Testing
- Verified builds for x64, ARM64, and ARM64EC architectures
- Confirmed UWP and Win32 build scenarios
- Validated security flag application across different configurations
- Tested JavaScript linting and formatting workflows

 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/microsoft/hermes-windows/pull/234)

## 🧩 이슈

<!-- 관련된 이슈 번호를 연결해주세요. 예: Closes #123 -->

<!--
| 키워드                   | 효과                          | 설명                                                                     |
| **Fixes #이슈번호**      | 해당 이슈를 **자동으로 닫음**          | PR 머지가 완료되면 **이슈가 자동으로 해결된 상태로 닫힙니다**.                                 |
| **Closes #이슈번호**     | 해당 이슈를 **자동으로 닫음**          | `Fixes`와 동일하게, PR 머지 시 해당 이슈가 자동으로 **완료** 처리됩니다.                       |
| **Resolves #이슈번호**   | 해당 이슈를 **자동으로 닫음**          | `Fixes`와 `Closes`와 동일한 효과로, **PR 머지 후 이슈가 해결되고 닫힘**.                   |
| **Related to #이슈번호** | 이슈와 **연결은 되지만 자동으로 닫히지 않음** | 해당 이슈와 관련이 있다는 것을 명시하고 싶을 때 사용. PR 머지 후 자동으로 닫히지 않으며, **단순히 연결만** 됩니다. |
| **Addresses #이슈번호**  | 이슈와 **연결되지만 자동으로 닫히지 않음**   | `Related to`와 비슷하게 **해당 이슈를 해결하는 PR임을 명시**하고 연결할 때 사용합니다.              |
| **Refs #이슈번호**       | 이슈와 **연결되지만 자동으로 닫히지 않음**   | 이슈와의 관계를 **참고용으로 추가**하고 싶은 경우 사용.                                      |
-->


- 예: `Closes #224`

body:
## Problem
Pages other than the home page (About, Services, Portfolio, Blog, Contact) were not center-aligned and lacked proper mobile responsiveness. The home page used proper centering classes while other pages were missing these critical CSS classes.

## Root Cause
The home page containers used:
```jsx
<div className="container mx-auto px-4 md:px-6 relative max-w-7xl">
```

While other pages were missing the centering classes:
```jsx
<div className="container px-4 md:px-6 relative">
```

## Solution
Added the missing `mx-auto` and `max-w-7xl` classes to all container elements across the affected pages to ensure consistent center alignment and responsive design.

## Changes Made
- **About page** (`app/about/page.tsx`) - Updated 5 container elements
- **Services page** (`app/services/page.tsx`) - Updated 4 container elements  
- **Portfolio page** (`app/portfolio/page.tsx`) - Updated 4 container elements
- **Blog page** (`app/blog/page.tsx`) - Updated 4 container elements
- **Contact page** (`app/contact/page.tsx`) - Updated 4 container elements

## Results
- ✅ All pages now have consistent center alignment matching the home page
- ✅ Mobile responsiveness verified on 375x667 viewport
- ✅ Footer navigation links maintain proper formatting
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality

## Screenshots

**Before (About page not centered):**
![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98834948-fb0c-447a-98b6-436b19f20b64)

**After (About page properly centered):**
![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81f129ce-e6fd-49c0-8adc-fa8c78287311)

**Mobile responsiveness (Contact page):**
![Mobile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ab6f51d-5e78-4cb0-a8d9-e4b4f0f834c7)

author: kazhuu
body:
The original documentation was okay, but could be improved. Also it had broken links that needs fixing. In this PR I fix the original broken links and update the documentation related to Nissan Leaf ZE1 models. I also added a lot more pictures of the process to make it more clear what needs to be done. Also added a troubleshooting section of the issue that has been asked multiple times on the discord server related to this firmware.

Feedback is welcome!

To test this:
* Go to the `docs` folder and run `make html`.
* Show the manual in the browser e.g. `firefox build/html/index.html`.

If you face 

```shell
/bin/sh: line 1: sphinx-build: command not found
make: *** [Makefile:20: html] Error 127
```
then install the `python3-sphinx` package e.g. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37757151/the-sphinx-build-command-was-not-found.

author: huffsamuel
body:
## What?
*Explain the changes you've made. It doesn't need to be fandy and you don't have to get technical.*

*Example:*
*I've added support for authentication. It includes model, table, controller, ant test. For more background, see #0*

## Why?
*Explain the goal this change achieves.*

*Example:*
*These changes complete the user login and account creation experience. See #0 for more information.*

## How?
*Draw attention to the significant design decisions of your changes. If you decided to write a recursive method instead of a loop, point out the merits of this to help reviewers understand your reasoning.*

*Example:*
This includes a migration, model, and controller for user authentication. I'm using a library to do the heavy lifting; migrations for the library are included here.*

## Testing?
*Indicate if this change includes tests. If any manual tests need to be performed, include steps for users to follow here.*

## Screenshots (optional)
*A simple screenshot of the before and after.*
*If your change isn't UI related, screenshots of .apk size, code layout, or other important information can help provide clarity to the result of the changes.*

## Anything Else?
*A space to call out potential architecture changes or technical debt. Call out challenges, optimizations, etc.*

*Example:*
*Let's consider using a 3rd party library to provide this feature so we can offload the technical details into a commonly used library that is well tested by the community.*
*Let's also consider breaking this out into its own library so we can re-use this code with other applications in the future.*

*Based on [Writing A Great Pull Request Description](https://www.pullrequest.com/blog/writing-a-great-pull-request-description/)

# Fix Date Input Corruption in Estimate Request Creation ## Summary Resolves the "作成に失敗しました" (Creation Failed) error when creating new estimate requests. The root cause was HTML `type="date"` input producing corrupted date values (e.g., "50815-02-02" instead of "2025-02-15"), causing backend validation failures. **Key Changes:** - Replaced HTML date input with text input accepting YYYY-MM-DD format - Added placeholder text to guide users: "YYYY-MM-DD (例: 2025-02-15)" - Simplified onChange handler to directly update React state - Removed complex date validation logic that was rejecting corrupted values **Testing Results:** - Successfully created estimate request with proper date format "2025-02-15" - Backend now correctly receives and processes date values - No more "無効な日付形式です" (Invalid date format) errors ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **End-to-end testing**: Create multiple estimate requests with different dates to ensure functionality works consistently - [ ] **Invalid date handling**: Test with invalid formats like "2025-13-40", "abc-def-ghi", and empty values to verify error handling - [ ] **Cross-browser compatibility**: Test in different browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) to confirm the date input corruption was not browser-specific - [ ] **User experience evaluation**: Assess whether the text input is acceptably user-friendly compared to the native date picker - [ ] **Backend validation**: Verify that the backend properly validates and rejects invalid date formats --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD Frontend["src/frontend/src/app/requests/page.tsx"]:::major-edit Backend["src/backend/src/handlers/requests.rs"]:::context Service["src/backend/src/services/estimate_request_service_impl.rs"]:::context Model["src/backend/src/models/estimate_request.rs"]:::context Database["PostgreSQL Database"]:::context Frontend -->|"POST /api/requests
deadline: 2025-02-15"| Backend Backend -->|"validate & process"| Service Service -->|"insert estimate_request"| Database Model -->|"defines schema"| Service subgraph Legend L1[Major Edit]:::major-edit L2[Minor Edit]:::minor-edit L3[Context/No Edit]:::context end classDef major-edit fill:#90EE90 classDef minor-edit fill:#87CEEB classDef context fill:#FFFFFF ``` ### Notes - **Hardcoded User ID**: The `created_by: 1` value is still hardcoded and will need proper authentication integration in the future - **Date Validation**: Consider adding client-side date validation to prevent invalid formats from being submitted - **Accessibility**: The native date input had built-in accessibility features that might be lost with the text input - **Alternative Solutions**: If the date input corruption is browser-specific, consider using a date picker library instead of reverting to text input **Session Info**: - Link to Devin run: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/51ade445b3af42eba22bfdea75500feb - Requested by: yasutaka.yamakawa.sa@mhi.com

body:
### **User description** This pull request introduces significant updates to the `ProgressRecordRepository` and `ProgressRecordService` classes, focusing on improving cache handling, adding support for reactivating deleted records, and enhancing repository methods. Key changes include the introduction of new repository methods, reworking cache invalidation, and improving error handling. ### Repository Enhancements * Added `findOneWithAnyStatus` and `findAnyByPlanIdAndDate` methods to the `ProgressRecordRepository` to support querying records regardless of their deletion status. These methods use `as unknown as ProgressRecord` to cast results to the appropriate type. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-da52377db3d688a2f21642dfda7348ff0449cb88078820ef11cd397fb413c087L71-R81) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-da52377db3d688a2f21642dfda7348ff0449cb88078820ef11cd397fb413c087L93-R134) * Updated existing repository methods (`create`, `findOne`, `findByPlanIdAndDate`, `update`, `remove`) to use `await` for consistency and added type casting for returned values. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-da52377db3d688a2f21642dfda7348ff0449cb88078820ef11cd397fb413c087L14-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-da52377db3d688a2f21642dfda7348ff0449cb88078820ef11cd397fb413c087L24-R24) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-da52377db3d688a2f21642dfda7348ff0449cb88078820ef11cd397fb413c087L83-R90) ### Service Enhancements * Replaced `validateUniqueRecord` with inline logic to handle reactivation of deleted records. If a record exists but is deleted, it is reactivated; otherwise, a conflict exception is thrown. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3896f78552af306ba890fe794b335997da6c9d23e3886c9ea26fdc7af41c8252L45-R69) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3896f78552af306ba890fe794b335997da6c9d23e3886c9ea26fdc7af41c8252L174-L180) * Enhanced the `update` method to support reactivating deleted records by introducing an `isReactivating` parameter and setting `is_deleted` to `false` when applicable. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3896f78552af306ba890fe794b335997da6c9d23e3886c9ea26fdc7af41c8252L92-R129) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3896f78552af306ba890fe794b335997da6c9d23e3886c9ea26fdc7af41c8252L110-R157) ### Cache Handling Improvements * Replaced `invalidateRecordCaches` with `invalidateAllRelatedCaches`, which now clears specific record caches, list caches, cessation plan caches, and leaderboard caches using wildcard patterns. Added detailed logging and error handling for cache operations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3896f78552af306ba890fe794b335997da6c9d23e3886c9ea26fdc7af41c8252L141-L147) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3896f78552af306ba890fe794b335997da6c9d23e3886c9ea26fdc7af41c8252L228-R321) * Updated cache set operations to use `setEx` for setting expiration and added error handling and logging for both cache retrieval and storage. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3896f78552af306ba890fe794b335997da6c9d23e3886c9ea26fdc7af41c8252R78-R110) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3896f78552af306ba890fe794b335997da6c9d23e3886c9ea26fdc7af41c8252L92-R129) ### Logging and Error Handling * Added debug logs for cache hits, cache misses, and cache invalidation operations to improve traceability. author: mohanson
body:
POSIX requires that opening a file with the O_APPEND flag should have no affect on the location at which pwrite() writes data. However, on Linux, if a file is opened with O_APPEND, pwrite() appends data to the end of the file, regardless of the value of offset.

See https://linux.die.net/man/2/pwrite.

author: arockwell
body:
## Summary
🚀 **Lightning-fast implementation of full vim modal editing in EMDX TUI\!**

This PR adds comprehensive vim-like keybindings to the edit mode, transforming the TUI into a powerful vim-style editor while maintaining EMDX's user-friendly design.

## 🎯 Key Features

### **Modal Editing System**
- **NORMAL** mode - Command and navigation mode
- **INSERT** mode - Text editing mode (default)
- **VISUAL** mode - Character-wise selection
- **VISUAL LINE** mode - Line-wise selection

### **Core Vim Commands**
- **Navigation**: `h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e` (word motions), `0/$` (line), `gg/G` (document)
- **Mode switching**: `i/a/I/A/o/O` (insert variants), `v/V` (visual modes)
- **Editing**: `x` (delete char), `dd` (delete line), `yy` (yank line), `p/P` (paste)
- **Repeat counts**: `3j`, `5w`, `2dd` etc.

### **Smart User Experience**
- Starts in **INSERT** mode (user expects to type immediately)
- **Dual ESC behavior**: `INSERT→NORMAL→EXIT` edit mode
- **Color-coded status bar**: Shows current mode and pending commands
- **Backward compatible**: Existing code continues to work

## 🏗️ Implementation Details

### **Architecture Excellence**
- Extends existing `EditTextArea` → `VimEditTextArea` 
- Leverages established modal patterns from browser navigation
- Integrates seamlessly with reactive state management
- Maintains the mount/unmount pattern for width constraints

### **Status Bar Integration**
```
EDIT MODE: #123 | -- INSERT -- | ESC for normal mode
EDIT MODE: #123 | -- NORMAL -- | ESC to save and exit  
EDIT MODE: #123 | -- NORMAL (3) -- | ESC to save and exit  # with repeat count
EDIT MODE: #123 | -- NORMAL (d) -- | ESC to save and exit   # pending command
```

### **Technical Highlights**
- Efficient word boundary detection with regex
- Direct text manipulation for reliable line operations
- Comprehensive key event handling with mode routing
- Safe cursor positioning with boundary checks

## ⚡ Why This Was So Fast

This feature was implemented in **record time** because:

1. **Solid Foundation** - The existing modal architecture provided the perfect base
2. **Clean Patterns** - The `SelectionTextArea` pattern made extension obvious  
3. **Good Planning** - Analysis documents provided a clear implementation roadmap
4. **Textual Framework** - Rich key handling made vim implementation smooth

## 🧪 Test Plan

- [x] Basic vim navigation (h/j/k/l) in normal mode
- [x] Mode transitions (i→INSERT, ESC→NORMAL, ESC→EXIT)
- [x] Word motions (w/b/e) and line navigation (0/$, gg/G)
- [x] Line operations (dd to delete, yy to yank, p to paste)
- [x] Status bar shows correct mode with color coding
- [x] Repeat counts work (3j moves down 3 lines)
- [x] Document switching blocked during edit mode
- [x] Proper width constraints after exiting edit mode

## 🎉 Result

A **powerful vim editing experience** that feels native to EMDX while preserving the user-friendly design philosophy. Power users get familiar vim commands, while casual users can still edit normally in INSERT mode.

**This proves that good architecture enables rapid feature development\!**

author: sanuthma
body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and refactors to the customer-facing features of the frontend, focusing on modularization, improved state management via custom hooks, and UI updates. The most notable changes include the addition of reusable hooks, a new `EditProfileModal` component, and updates to the sidebar and dashboard card styles.

### Modularization and State Management Enhancements:
* **Custom Hooks**: Introduced several reusable hooks, such as `useCustomerSidebar`, `useCustomerModals`, `useMedicalRecords`, and `useMedicalRecordDetail`, to encapsulate state management logic and improve code reusability. (`frontend/src/features/customer/hooks/index.js`, `frontend/src/features/customer/hooks/useCustomerSidebar.js`, `frontend/src/features/customer/hooks/useCustomerModals.js`, `frontend/src/features/customer/hooks/useMedicalRecords.js`, `frontend/src/features/customer/hooks/useMedicalRecordDetail.js`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c532b7dacf761feb1e5452f81dd8e2be436443991e43a33235fb48e3403a180eR1-R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-37055fe661daa93a4cc6c91ab043f910af8e26de463625b4daaee6251e077b86R1-R45) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9043c8f69c1b2b6ab220e4ae17c4b065676603ad6f131266d417771d625924a1R1-R40) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-008d291ee2a2ab6ac3df59b2cbbbdf71e358f596dd7fa3d235387105a5348a41R1-R83) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-89c23e1a5b6a3bdf2f3359cda00e83720c0df9afb556769ef394bc89b3db92c7R1-R88)

### Component Enhancements:
* **EditProfileModal Component**: Added a new `EditProfileModal` component with extensive form handling, validation, and accessibility features, such as focus trapping and keyboard navigation. It supports editing personal, medical, and emergency contact information. (`frontend/src/features/customer/components/EditProfileModal.jsx`)

### Refactoring and Cleanup:

author: avenger-285714
body:
On some external USB hard drives, mounting can fail if "lshw" is executed during the process.

This occurs because data sent to the device's output endpoint in certain abnormal scenarios does not receive a response, leading to a mount timeout.

[ Description of "use_192_bytes_for_3f" in the kernel code: ]
  /*
   * Many disks only accept MODE SENSE transfer lengths of
   * 192 bytes (that's what Windows uses). */ sdev->use_192_bytes_for_3f = 1;

The kernel's SCSI driver, when handling devices with this attribute, sends commands with a length of 192 bytes like this:
  if (sdp->use_192_bytes_for_3f)
  	res = sd_do_mode_sense(sdp, 0, 0x3F, buffer, 192, &data, NULL);

However, "lshw" disregards the "use_192_bytes_for_3f" attribute and transmits data with a length of 0xff bytes via ioctl, which can cause some hard drives to hang and become unusable.

To resolve this issue, prevent commands with a length of 0xff bytes from being queued via ioctl when it detects the "use_192_bytes_for_3f" attribute on the device.

The hard drive device identified with the issue is Lenovo USB 17ef:4531. Tested on HONOR NBLK-WAX9X (C234) Notebook with AMD Ryzen 7 3700U.

author: novinbukannopin
body:
This pull request introduces a token-based authentication system, including middleware for validating and refreshing tokens, a gRPC service for token validation, and enhancements to the HTTP API for user authentication. It also adds JWT support and refactors dependency injection for better modularity.

### Authentication System Enhancements:

* **Middleware for Token Validation and Refreshing**: Added `MiddlewareValidateAuth` and `MiddlewareRefreshToken` in `cmd/middleware.go` to handle authentication and token expiration checks.
* **JWT Token Handling**: Implemented `GenerateToken` and `ValidateToken` functions in `helpers/jwt.go` to create and validate JWT tokens using `golang-jwt`.

### gRPC Service Integration:

* **Token Validation gRPC Service**: Added `TokenValidation` service with `ValidateToken` RPC in `cmd/proto/token_validation/token_validation.proto` and corresponding generated files (`token_validation.pb.go`, `token_validation_grpc.pb.go`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2c45cd4251f21b40a45685e1129876cd6d273697435c942024a0f7b1f67c0409R1-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-320c9196871805b26567b48abf3aa0066443dedb7ea406b63eaee7c2ee0ccb6fR1-R248) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9fd456ede13239b80eaf0ff96ebd382b34a7a5b01ebd3f1a2eb90efb473012ebR1-R121)
* **gRPC Server Registration**: Updated `cmd/gprc.go` to register the `TokenValidationServer`.

### HTTP API Enhancements:

* **User Authentication Endpoints**: Added routes for login, logout, token refresh, and health check in `cmd/http.go`. These routes utilize the new DI container for dependency injection.
* **Login API**: Implemented `LoginHandler` in `internal/api/login.go` to handle user login requests and return authentication tokens.

### Dependency and Configuration Updates:

* **Dependency Injection Refactor**: Introduced `DIContainer` in `cmd/http.go` to centralize service and repository dependencies.
* **New Dependencies**: Added `golang-jwt`, `pkg/errors`, and `x/crypto` to `go.mod` for JWT handling and error management. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-33ef32bf6c23acb95f5902d7097b7a1d5128ca061167ec0716715b0b9eeaa5f6R8-R12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-33ef32bf6c23acb95f5902d7097b7a1d5128ca061167ec0716715b0b9eeaa5f6L38)

author: thancode99382
body:
This pull request introduces two new components, `PaymentAnalytics` and `PaymentDetail`, to enhance the admin payments dashboard with analytics and detailed transaction views. These components provide visual insights into payment data and allow for detailed exploration of individual transactions.

### Payment Analytics Enhancements:
* Added `PaymentAnalytics` component to display key metrics (e.g., average revenue per transaction, most popular payment method, failure rate) using `Card` components. It includes mock data for demonstration purposes.
* Integrated various chart types (`AreaChart`, `DonutChart`, `BarChart`, `LineChart`) to visualize trends in revenue, payment methods, transaction statuses, and transaction volumes.
* Introduced utility functions `formatCurrency` and `valueFormatter` for consistent currency formatting across the component.

### Payment Detail Enhancements:
* Added `PaymentDetail` component to provide an interactive modal for viewing detailed information about a specific payment transaction, including status, customer details, financial breakdown, and timeline.
* Implemented actions for refunding completed transactions, retrying failed transactions, and copying transaction/order IDs to the clipboard.
* Introduced a status configuration system to dynamically render transaction statuses with appropriate labels, icons, and styles.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The `IPreProfessionalInternshipService` was incorrectly implemented as a concrete class with an interface naming convention, causing build failures and violating .NET architectural patterns.

**Issues:**
- Class named with "I" prefix but was a concrete implementation, not an interface
- Registered incorrectly in DI container: `AddScoped<IPreProfessionalInternshipService, IPreProfessionalInternshipService>()`
- Tests failed with error: `'IPreProfessionalInternshipService' does not contain a constructor that takes 2 arguments`
- Violated interface segregation and dependency inversion principles

## Solution

Implemented proper interface/implementation separation following .NET conventions:

### Changes Made

1. **Created proper interface** (`/Interfaces/Services/IPreProfessionalInternshipService.cs`):
   ```csharp
   public interface IPreProfessionalInternshipService
   {
       Task<List<PreProfessionalInternshipDto>> GetAllAsync();
       Task<List<PreProfessionalInternshipDto>> GetFilteredAsync(FilterPreProfessionalInternshipDto filters);
   }
   ```

2. **Renamed and moved concrete implementation** (`/Services/PreProfessionalInternshipService.cs`):
   ```csharp
   public class PreProfessionalInternshipService : IPreProfessionalInternshipService
   ```

3. **Fixed dependency injection registration** (`Program.cs`):
   ```csharp
   // Before (incorrect)
   builder.Services.AddScoped<IPreProfessionalInternshipService, IPreProfessionalInternshipService>();
   
   // After (correct)
   builder.Services.AddScoped<IPreProfessionalInternshipService, PreProfessionalInternshipService>();
   ```

4. **Updated test constructor** to use concrete implementation:
   ```csharp
   _service = new PreProfessionalInternshipService(_repositoryMock.Object);
   ```

## Results

- ✅ **Build**: 0 errors (was 1 error)
- ✅ **Tests**: All 55 tests passing
- ✅ **Architecture**: Proper interface/implementation separation
- ✅ **No breaking changes** to existing functionality

## Impact

This fix ensures:
- Proper dependency injection patterns
- Testable and maintainable code architecture
- Adherence to .NET naming conventions and SOLID principles
- Foundation for future service implementations

author: sunyuhan1998
body:
As mentioned in the issue #3786 , when using embedding models, we need to support the `encodingFormat=base64` parameter. When this format is used, the model returns the `embedding` field as a base64-encoded string representing a float array. This PR adds support for handling that format.

**Changes in this PR:**

1. Introduced a custom JSON deserializer, `OpenAiEmbeddingDeserializer`, for the `embedding` field in `org.springframework.ai.openai.api.OpenAiApi.Embedding`. This deserializer automatically converts the base64-encoded string back into a float array when parsing the API response.
2. Added corresponding unit tests.

Fixes: #3786

author: dubianhaozhi
body:
Fixes #36

## Summary
- Fixed timezone conversion bug causing schedule dates to shift by one day
- Parent view was showing holidays as registered and correct dates as unregistered
- Used `zonedTimeToUtc()` from `date-fns-tz` to properly convert JST dates to UTC

## Changes
- Fixed single schedule creation form
- Fixed multi-schedule creation form
- Fixed schedule update forms
- Added proper JST timezone handling throughout

author: kargnas
body:
## Problems

### Issue 1: additionalProperties Schema Compatibility
The Gemini API does not support the `additionalProperties` field in JSON schemas, causing HTTP 400 errors when using ObjectSchema instances with this field.

### Issue 2: Thinking Token Exhaustion Detection
Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash models consume significant thinking tokens (200-450+) during structured output generation, causing token exhaustion with low `maxTokens` values and resulting in empty array responses with unclear error messages.

## Root Causes

### Schema Compatibility Issue
The `SchemaMap` class was including the `additionalProperties` field from ObjectSchema in API requests, which Gemini rejects with:
```
Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "additionalProperties"
```

### Silent Token Exhaustion Issue
When users specify low token limits (e.g., 200 tokens), thinking tokens consume almost all available tokens, leaving no room for actual structured output generation. This results in `finishReason: "MAX_TOKENS"` and empty response content with no clear indication of the root cause.

## Solutions

### Fix 1: Schema Compatibility
```php
// Remove additionalProperties for Gemini compatibility
$schemaArray = $this->schema->toArray();
unset($schemaArray['additionalProperties']);
```

### Fix 2: Clear Error Detection and Messaging
```php
// Check for thinking token exhaustion pattern
$finishReason = data_get($data, 'candidates.0.finishReason');
$content = data_get($data, 'candidates.0.content.parts.0.text', '');
$thoughtTokens = data_get($data, 'usageMetadata.thoughtsTokenCount', 0);

if ($finishReason === 'MAX_TOKENS' && empty(trim($content)) && $thoughtTokens > 0) {
    throw PrismException::providerResponseError(
        'Gemini thinking tokens exhausted the token limit, leaving no tokens for structured output generation. ' .
        'Try increasing maxTokens to account for thinking overhead (suggested: 2-3x current value).'
    );
}
```

## Implementation Details

### Clear Error Messages
- **Detection**: Identifies thinking token exhaustion pattern automatically
- **Guidance**: Provides specific solution (2-3x token increase)
- **User-friendly**: Clear explanation of root cause and fix
- **No cost impact**: Doesn't automatically increase tokens, lets user decide

### Schema Processing
- Removes unsupported `additionalProperties` field before API calls
- Maintains full ObjectSchema API compatibility
- Preserves all other schema features

## Testing & Verification

### Before Fix
```php
// With maxTokens: 200
$response->structured = []; // Empty array with no clear error
$response->usage->completionTokens = 0; // No output generated
```

### After Fix
```php
// Same request now throws clear error:
// "Gemini thinking tokens exhausted the token limit, leaving no tokens 
//  for structured output generation. Try increasing maxTokens to account 
//  for thinking overhead (suggested: 2-3x current value)."
```

## Impact

This comprehensive fix resolves both major Gemini structured output issues:
- **Schema compatibility**: ObjectSchema with `allowAdditionalProperties` now works
- **Error clarity**: Users get clear guidance when thinking tokens cause issues
- **Cost awareness**: No automatic token increases, user maintains control
- **Backward compatibility**: No breaking changes to existing code

author: davenpi
body:
## What changed?

Added a `MessageCoordinator` for the client and tested it thoroughly.

## Why?

- Adopt the pattern we learned refactoring the server session.
- First step in moving away from `BaseSession` (can't use it for server so we're going to dump it)

## Impact

- Makes code base more consistent and provides a cleaner separation of concerns.

## Testing

Added extensive tests for the coordinator and improved existing ones for the server coordinator as well.

## Review notes

N/A

## Checklist

- [x] All new and old tests pass
- [x] Code follows our style guidelines
- [x] Documentation updated if needed
- [x] Breaking changes documented in commit messages

author: nerixyz
body:
Sometimes, it's useful to be able to pass extra arguments to the invocation. My use-case is to be able to load Clazy (Qt clang-tidy checks) as a plugin through `-load`. This PR adds `extra_arguments` which is appended to the invocation (split with `shlex.split`).

Closes #89.

## Summary

Implements **TASK 1.2: gRPC Communication Layer** from the Tapio Mega Epic, delivering a production-ready streaming communication system capable of handling 165,000+ events per second with enterprise-grade reliability.

### Core Deliverables ✅

- **proto/collector.proto**: Complete gRPC service definitions with bidirectional streaming
- **pkg/grpc/server.go**: High-performance streaming server with backpressure handling  
- **pkg/grpc/client.go**: Resilient client with automatic reconnection and exponential backoff
- **pkg/grpc/batching.go**: Efficient event batching system for maximum throughput
- **pkg/grpc/flow_control.go**: Sophisticated flow control with token bucket rate limiting
- **pkg/grpc/connection.go**: Connection pooling and lifecycle management

### Performance Achievements 🚀

- **165k+ events/sec** throughput capability validated through comprehensive benchmarks
- **<10ms end-to-end latency** for event processing
- **<50MB memory usage** for streaming buffers with backpressure controls
- **Zero-allocation design** with object pooling and lock-free data structures
- **Multiple compression algorithms** (LZ4, Gzip, Zstd, Snappy) for bandwidth optimization

### Enterprise Features 🏢

- **Automatic reconnection** with exponential backoff for network resilience
- **Health checking** and connection monitoring with configurable timeouts
- **Per-connection and global rate limiting** with burst allowance
- **Memory-aware backpressure** with graceful degradation under load
- **Connection pooling** and load balancing support for horizontal scaling
- **Graceful shutdown** and comprehensive resource cleanup

### Validation & Testing 🧪

- **pkg/grpc/performance_test.go**: Complete benchmark suite validating target performance
- **examples/grpc_streaming/main.go**: Working demo showcasing all streaming features
- **Integration tests** covering streaming scenarios and failure modes
- **Memory usage validation** and connection lifecycle testing

### Technical Highlights 🔧

- **Bidirectional streaming** with flow control and backpressure
- **Token bucket rate limiting** with per-connection controls
- **Event batching** with configurable size and timeout thresholds
- **Connection management** with automatic cleanup and health monitoring
- **Compression support** with multiple algorithms for different scenarios
- **Metrics integration** for monitoring and observability

## Test Plan

- [x] Run performance benchmarks: `go test -bench=. ./pkg/grpc/...`
- [x] Execute integration tests: `go test ./pkg/grpc/...`
- [x] Validate demo functionality: `go run examples/grpc_streaming/main.go`
- [x] Check memory usage under load
- [x] Verify reconnection behavior with network interruptions
- [x] Test backpressure mechanisms with high throughput

This implementation provides the foundational communication layer for the Tapio observability platform, enabling real-time event streaming between eBPF collectors and the central server with production-grade reliability.

author: calghar
body:
Fixes #3742

### Description
This PR clarifies the scope of `denylist` and `allowlist` export filters in the Tetragon documentation. Users were confused about why filtered events still appeared in `tetra` CLI output, not realizing these filters only apply to JSON file exports and not to gRPC streaming.

The changes add:
- A prominent caution note in `docs/content/en/docs/events.md` using the `{{< caution >}}` shortcode to clearly explain that export filters only affect JSON file sinks
- Concise inline notes in the Helm chart value tables in both `helm-chart.md` and `README.md` to indicate the filters are "for file sinks only"

These documentation updates will help users understand the intended behavior and avoid confusion when using the `tetra` CLI alongside export filters.

### Changelog
```release-note
docs: Clarify that export filters (denylist/allowlist) only apply to JSON file exports, not gRPC streaming
```

These changes replace the formula for accuracy pp, as well as penalise rhythm difficulty from pp based on estimated unstable rate.

More effort has been put in to balance this than my other recent changes. The new curve is steeper than the current (making improving your acc on a play more rewarding) and attempts to break even with the current curve at 98% accuracy on a nomod map of the given star rating, based on estimated UR data from a large number of ranked maps. See said data and how the curves compare here https://www.desmos.com/calculator/hwd2pjmqqr

The rhythm penalty uses the same data but for 100% acc rather than 98% to estimate the unstable rate at which all of a map's rhythm difficulty has been played successfully. 2x this unstable rate is around 90-91% on the same maps which is where I think it's safe to say all rhythm difficulty has been ignored. `Rhythm difficulty / star rating` has been a good measure of rhythm contribution to a map since https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/32426, with around 0.15 being where rhythm starts to have any effect on star rating and 0.35 being maps like 3772247 (hard rhythm but mechanically easy) and 4543374 (very hard rhythm). Removing all rhythm strain from these 0.35 maps reduces star rating by ~20%, and doing the same on maps in the middle with 0.25 (such as 3658314 and 4725197) reduces star rating by ~5% which is why I went with `0.2 * rhythmFactor^2` for the penalty's max value.

I also renamed the mono acc scaling stuff for more clarity now that we have two acc related scalings in difficulty pp

## What kind of change does this PR introduce?

This PR adds SIWE (Sign-In-With-Ethereum) support to auth-js, related to [this PR on /auth](https://github.com/supabase/auth/pull/2069)

## What is the current behavior?

Multiple providers & SIWS (Solana) supported

## What is the new behavior?

Add SIWE (Ethereum) support.

## Additional context

The types are inspired by the the [viem](https://viem.sh/) library, which has minimal & modern types, but they were simplified and copied over to the local code to remove dependency on it.

author: 0xviva
body:
### Adding a system set

This is a PR for this issue: https://github.com/TotalKrill/bevy_ui_anchor/issues/10

**Reason for this PR:**

This is useful for cases where I want to run other systems in the same schedule but before the UI anchor runs. Say my game has physics and I want to move a player label after the physics set called sync. 

I had this issue in my game where the attached UI anchor was lagging behind the moving character because the system `system_move_ui_nodes` in your plugin is running in a _later_ schedule than the `PhysicsSet::Sync` from [Avian ](https://github.com/Jondolf/avian) which im on my shared player movement and move camera system. 

So making a system set like this that I can put in the ordering constraints `.before()` or `.after()` after my desired systems is really helpful.

### Example of how to use this SystemSet:

```rust
app.add_systems(
    PostUpdate,
    (
        shared::move_players.after(movement::player_movement),
        move_camera,
    )
        .chain()
        .after(PhysicsSet::Sync)
        .before(AnchorUiSystemSet::MoveUiNodes) // <-------
        .before(TransformSystem::TransformPropagate),
);
```

Hope this PR finds you great @TotalKrill.

author: ltxworld
body:
## Summary

This pull request adds full support for the `linux/riscv64` architecture, enabling users on RISC-V platforms to build and install `g` seamlessly.

## Changes Made

1.  **`Makefile`**:
    * A `build-linux-riscv64` target has been added to cross-compile for the RISC-V 64-bit architecture.
    * This new target has been added as a dependency to the `build-linux` meta-target, integrating it into the `make build-all` release process.

2.  **`install.sh`**:
    * The `get_arch()` function has been updated to correctly identify the `riscv64` architecture by checking the output of `uname -m`. This allows the automated installation script to download the correct pre-compiled binary for RISC-V users.

## Test

To ensure the validity of these changes, I have performed end-to-end testing on my RISC-V development board.

- **Hardware**:LicheePi4A 8+64G
- **OS**: RevyOS 20250420

**Test Scenarios:**

**Manual Deployment Test**:
    - **Action**: Cross-compiled the `g` binary using the modified `Makefile`,use `make build-linux-riscv64`.
    - **Result**: The binary was successfully transferred to the RISC-V borad and ran correctly after manual configuration. The `g install 1.24.2` command executed without errors.

```bash
debian@revyos-lpi4a:~$ g install 1.24.2
Downloading 100% [===============] (76/76 MB, 6.6 MB/s)
Computing checksum with SHA256
Checksums matched
Now using go1.24.2 linux/riscv64
```

body:
This pull request introduces a Django-based backend and a React-based frontend for the OctoFit Tracker project. The backend includes database models, RESTful APIs, and administrative functionality, while the frontend is set up with Create React App. Below is a summary of the key changes:

### Backend Changes

#### Core Backend Setup:
* Added `manage.py` to handle Django administrative tasks. (`octofit-tracker/backend/manage.py`)
* Configured Django settings with MongoDB as the database using `djongo`. (`octofit-tracker/backend/octofit_tracker/settings.py`)

#### Models and Database:
* Defined models for `User`, `Team`, `Activity`, `Leaderboard`, and `Workout` using `djongo`. (`octofit-tracker/backend/octofit_tracker/models.py`)

#### API and Serialization:
* Implemented serializers for all models to enable JSON serialization and deserialization. (`octofit-tracker/backend/octofit_tracker/serializers.py`)
* Created viewsets and an API root endpoint for RESTful access to the models. (`octofit-tracker/backend/octofit_tracker/views.py`)
* Configured URL routing for the API and admin panel. (`octofit-tracker/backend/octofit_tracker/urls.py`)

#### Database Population:
* Added a custom management command to populate the database with test data for all models. (`octofit-tracker/backend/octofit_tracker/management/commands/populate_db.py`)

### Frontend Changes

#### Core Frontend Setup:
* Initialized a React project using Create React App with a basic `index.html` and manifest configuration. (`octofit-tracker/frontend/public/index.html`, `octofit-tracker/frontend/public/manifest.json`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8b7fcba1ac5a9da49446832c2d56bd37ed6c6fefe802bf34dd56045c56c40985R1-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-eb2a974c6ba7783e44c52c1253eba8b9d09f3a9b04fd6cdb7c896b39fab60795R1-R25)
* Added a `package.json` file with dependencies like React, React Router, and Bootstrap. (`octofit-tracker/frontend/package.json`)

#### Miscellaneous:
* Added `.gitignore` for the frontend to exclude build files, environment files, and logs. (`octofit-tracker/frontend/.gitignore`)
* Included a README file with instructions for running and building the frontend. (`octofit-tracker/frontend/README.md`)

### Additional Changes

* Added `requirements.txt` to specify Python dependencies for the backend, including Django, `djongo`, and `djangorestframework`. (`octofit-tracker/backend/requirements.txt`)
* Configured ASGI and WSGI files for deployment. (`octofit-tracker/backend/octofit_tracker/asgi.py`, `octofit-tracker/backend/octofit_tracker/wsgi.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dd406aa4c457a19bb9e197c161f52df5f790dc3c4f217003767b3021301f10d0R1-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3e0ccbfd477a2ec034d3b11b67a0ff90189433fb2c43359855cfd5d155f07d22R1-R16)

author: erikgrinaker
body:
## Problem

The communicator gRPC client currently attempts to pipeline GetPage requests from multiple callers onto the same gRPC stream. This has a number of issues:

* Head-of-line blocking: the request may block on e.g. layer download or LSN wait, delaying the next request.
* Cancellation: we can't easily cancel in-progress requests (e.g. due to timeout or backend termination), so it may keep blocking the next request (even its own retry).
* Complex stream scheduling: picking a stream becomes harder/slower, and additional Tokio tasks and synchronization is needed for stream management.

Touches #11735.
Requires #12579.

## Summary of changes

This patch removes pipelining of gRPC stream requests, and instead prefers to scale out the number of streams to achieve the same throughput. Stream scheduling has been rewritten, and mostly follows the same pattern as the client pool with exclusive acquisition by a single caller.

[Benchmarks](https://github.com/neondatabase/neon/pull/12583) show that the cost of an idle server-side GetPage worker task is about 26 KB (2.5 GB for 100,000), so we can afford to scale out.

This has a number of advantages:

* It (mostly) eliminates head-of-line blocking (except at the TCP level).
* Cancellation becomes trivial, by closing the stream.
* Stream scheduling becomes significantly simpler and cheaper.
* Individual callers can still use client-side batching for pipelining.

body: See https://manipulation.csail.mit.edu/robot.html for the newer, preferred implementation. Closes #14992. --- The `manipulation_station` example pulls in model files (iiwa, wsg, ycb) as mandatory data dependencies of pydrake, which means every bazel downstream project that uses `@drake//bindings/pydrake` has its runfiles bloated by stuff it doesn't need. Since we already have good examples of the preferred Python way to do this (and more coming later this year), and we consider this C++ code a dis-preferred pattern, best to just remove it now. Since the `examples` code is not [Stable API](https://drake.mit.edu/stable.html), we don't need a deprecation period. - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/RobotLocomotion/drake/23182)

## Description

This PR sets up and tests the Event Management functionality for the CharityConnect backend. It includes:

- 🛠 Initial implementation of event creation (`POST /api/events/create`)
- 🔍 Event retrieval with filters (`GET /api/events/get`)
  - Supports `type`, `search`, `location`, `supportgroup`, `category`
- 📄 Fetch single event by ID (`GET /api/events/get/:id`)
- 👤 Populates creator info (`org_name`, `org_profilepic`)

## Purpose

This PR is **not final** — it is created to:
- Test the endpoints during frontend integration
- Debug response format, population issues, and seat handling
- Identify and resolve API/data issues (like ObjectId casting, empty filters, etc.)

## Next Steps

- [ ] Improve error handling for invalid IDs
- [ ] Add unit tests (optional)
- [ ] Add memory and registration integration
- [ ] Finalize filtering logic and validation

## How to Test

Use Postman or frontend to test:
- POST /api/events/create
- GET /api/events/get
- GET /api/events/get/:id

Check:
- JSON structure
- Population of `creator_id`
- Filtering behavior

---

This PR is open for review and feedback. Testing actively in progress. ✅
